annotation.title_clean: Robot-First Mars Settlement: A Conceptual Framework for Technology Governance, Risk Reduction, and Interplanetary Policy
annotation.title_en: Robot-First Mars Settlement: A Conceptual Framework for Technology Governance, Risk Reduction, and Interplanetary Policy
annotation.venue: Innovation Journal of Social Sciences and Economic Review
annotation.summary_en: Conceptual paper proposing a robot-first Mars settlement model in which about 10,000 autonomous swarm robots, governed by AI under human strategic oversight, build and test habitats before humans arrive. It stresses accountability, auditability, planetary protection and compliance with the Outer Space Treaty.
key_provisions_or_claims: Deploy ~10,000-robot self-organizing swarm to validate Martian infrastructure before human arrival
Human arrival is conditional on readiness thresholds (e.g., 95% energy uptime, 24-72h failure recovery)
Human oversight operates at strategic/normative level; governance parameters embedded in AI objectives
Autonomy must be governed via transparent rules, auditability and defined human responsibility
Framework aligned with Outer Space Treaty and COSPAR planetary protection
